Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1587; not left out, i.e. (by implication) inexhaustible:--that faileth not.
BiblicalUsage: Jesus tells His disciples to provide bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not. The word describes a treasure that never runs out, that no thief approaches and no moth corrupts.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for a treasure that never fails carries no teaching of its own; its comfort is Jesus', that what we lay up in heaven is the only wealth that cannot be lost.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
